tools.description: This computer's cap on live coding sessions: cap (null when none), used (live Claude Code and Codex processes, managed or not, whose folder was written within the last 30 minutes), free, at_capacity, total and quiet (quiet ones are not counted), degraded when the process table could not be read. switchboard dispatch answers state refused with reason at_capacity (and used, cap) while the pool is full, and launch --hosted is refused: a wait, not a failed run; ask again when a session ends. cap sets the cap (1 to 500), clear removes it; without either, reads only. Setting or clearing it only when the operator asks.
tools.name: switchboard_capacity
tools.title: Session pool

tools.description: The session duty officer: every five minutes it looks at each live interactive Claude Code session on this computer (not Fabric Dashboards' consoles, not claude -p runs) and never ends one before it finished. Finished: idle for idle_minutes (default 60, never under 65 so a session waiting for a wake-up it set itself is kept) with none of its own commands (Bash tool shells, background ones included) still running: closed. Stalled: busy with its status unchanged and its transcript unwritten for stuck_minutes (45), its process tree using no CPU since the previous check, and no command of its own running (or one running three times stuck_minutes without CPU): closed and resumed in a new Terminal window with claude --resume and a prompt to continue. A session waiting for the person's answer is left alone, nothing is restarted for its age, and of two copies of one session only a finished copy is closed. At most three actions a check and three restarts of one session in six hours. Answers settings, due (what a check would do now), recent (its last actions), watched, waiting_for_person and running_commands. on, stuck_minutes, idle_minutes and run (check now) change it (waiting_minutes and max_age_hours are kept for older settings and unused); dry_run lists without acting.
tools.name: switchboard_duty
tools.title: Session duty officer

tools.description: Continue a session that ended (closed by the duty officer, its window closed after an idle hour, stopped on a limit) as that same session: claude --resume in its own Claude config folder and its folder, in a Terminal window of its own, so its history and context are the ones it had. Refused while a process still holds it, when its folder or history is gone, and for a session Switchboard has no record of. sessions with rows names the sessions that can be continued (act continue).
tools.name: switchboard_session_continue
tools.title: Continue a session as itself

tools.description: The state of a restart wave, the newest when wave is left out: each session pending (waiting for its turn to end), ending, resuming, back (a new process holds it), continuing (yours, working again), failed with the reason (not_back, still_running, host_refused, host_gone, not_started, not_written, cannot_resume, gone), skipped with the reason (still_busy after a day, changed_since_plan) or cancelled; counts; done_at once nothing is left to do.
tools.name: switchboard_sessions_restart_status
tools.title: A restart wave's state

tools.description: Sessions Switchboard launched: Claude Code, Codex, Kimi Code, Hermes, OpenCode and catalog agents (through an API-key account's proxy or on the OpenRouter key). Each with account_id, label, agent (the catalog id, such as claude-code, codex or goose), provider (the provider the route serves: claude for an agent through the proxy), group id (pool), context (personal or org:<id>) and context_name (the organization's name, or null), mode (managed or isolated), working_directory, in_place, launched_at, started_at, continues (a workflow id or null) and state: starting, running, ended or unknown. Without all, only starting and running ones. With history, every launch of the last 90 days instead, newest first: one record per launch with launch_id, launched_by (surface: window, cli, mcp, fallback, recovery, dashboards or fabric for a run switchboard dispatch started, whose launched_by.dispatch is {id, request, thread, project, workflow}; caller_launch_id, caller_project, caller_program, by, parent), provider_session_id, transcript (its path), turns, last_turn_at, ended (limit; a dispatched run's {kind: exited, stopped or timed_out, exit_code?, at}) and continued_as (where its work went), and for a dispatched run log (its log file's absolute path), plus total and next_before (pass it as before for the next page; null at the end; limit 1 to 500, default 500). With launch_id, that launch with up (who launched it, to the first) and down (what it launched or what took its work over). Reads only; no credential. With tree, the session tree instead: every live session joined to its launch (surface, parent launch, task: workflow and board request), the launches of the last day with their state (running, ended, gone), counts by group and surface, the session pool, and what the one-minute watch found (duplicate: one session in two processes; stuck: a board run quiet for 30 minutes; gone: a launch whose process ended with no end recorded).

before.description: With history: only launches started before this time, Unix seconds: the previous page's next_before.

history.description: Every recorded launch, newest first, instead of the homes' current sessions.

limit.description: With history: at most this many launches (default 500).

rows.description: This computer's sessions as one list in four groups (needs_you, running, waiting, ended), each row with its agent, account, folder, origin and the acts it has (close_copy, attach, end, continue).

tree.description: Every live session joined to its launch (surface, parent, task, group, account), the last day's launches with who started whom, counts by group and surface, and the one-minute watch's findings (duplicate, stuck, gone).
